messages:
anna: Quick q — how does the gateway pick a winner when we have a host wildcard, a more specific host, and a header-based override?

anna: Example config:
```
- id: r1
  host: "*.api.redwood.com"
  path: "/v1/*"
  svc: service-a
- id: r2
  host: "payments.api.redwood.com"
  path: "/v1/payments/*"
  svc: service-b
- id: r3
  host: "*.api.redwood.com"
  path: "/v1/payments/internal/*"
  headers:
    X-Internal: "true"
  svc: service-c
```

anna: If a request comes for payments.api.redwood.com /v1/payments/internal/xyz with header `X-Internal: true`, which route should win? r2 (more specific host+path) or r3 (header override + more specific path but less specific host)?

jasper: IMO deterministic rule we used earlier was: host specificity > path specificity > header specificity. So r2 wins. But I get why internal/header routes should be preferred to avoid leaking internal endpoints.

rohit: We had a similar debate last year — we resolved by preferring "security scoped" routes (headers/auth) when there's any overlap that could expose protected endpoints. So r3 should win in that policy.

infra-bot: lint: routing.yaml: duplicate-candidate warning between r2 and r3 — no explicit priority set. Recommend adding `priority` to one.

jasper: Proposal: add numeric `priority` optional field. Default computed as `(host_score * 1000) + (path_score * 10) + header_score`. Host_score: exact host=10, subdomain exact=8, wildcard suffix=5. Path_score: literal segment=3, wildcard=1. header_score: exact header match=10, none=0. That keeps backward compatibility but lets config authors override.

anna: Numeric priority makes sense. But many teams rely on implicit logic. Can we also have a deterministic tie-breaker that prefers "more restrictive" routes (headers, auth) when priority ties? Safer default.

rohit: Agree. Also edge-case: regex capture vs literal. A regex `/v1/(.*)` should lose to literal `/v1/payments` even if regex compiled earlier. So path_score should heavily weight literal tokens.

jasper: I'll draft an RFC and a matcher change. Plan: (1) compute default priority, (2) tie-breaker: restrictiveness (headers/auth > none), (3) final tie-break by config creation order. I'll add lint warnings for ambiguous sets. @anna @rohit drop test cases and I'll land a small PR.

anna: I'll add 3 tests to `tests/matcher` — header-wins, literal-path-wins, host-exact-wins. Also will add a short note in the Console docs to show computed priority.

rohit: :thumbsup: thanks — that should cover most ambiguity. We should also log which rule matched in traces so customers can debug.

sre-oncall: Note: ensure fallbacks still respect SLA routing (don't route to slow fallback just because it's more specific). Keep smart routing in the loop.

jasper: good call — I'll include routing cost heuristics as a future extension in the RFC.
